properties.publicTransport: Routes 441, 504 and 506 will be diverting while road closures are in place. Visit transportnsw.info to plan your trip.
properties.otherAdvice:
Thousands of participants will take part in the 5km and 10km Mother's Day Classic fun run and walk events starting from 7am in The Domain. Participants will travel along sections of Macquarie St, College St then Art Gallery Rd and Mrs Macquarie's Rd to finish back in The Domain by approximately 12pm.

Mother's Day is traditionally one of the busiest days on the roads. Wherever you are travelling, expect it to take longer than usual and factor in extra travel time. 

ROAD CLOSURES

  • 5am to 12pm midday: Art Gallery Rd/Mrs Macquarie's Rd from Prince Albert Rd. 
  • 5am to 10.30am: Hospital Rd and a section of Prince Albert Rd. Access to Sydney Hospital and Hospital Rd is via Shakespeare Pl only in both directions.
  • 6am to 10.30am: Macquarie St between St James Rd and Hunter St, College St between Park St and Prince Albert Rd and sections of St James Rd, Prince Albert Rd, St Mary's Rd and Yurong Pkwy will be closed.

Special event clearways will be in effect from 5am to 10.30am on sections of Macquarie St, Hunter St, College St, Prince Albert Rd, St Mary's Rd and St James Rd. Clearways will also be in effect on sections of Prince Albert Rd and Hospital Rd from 5am to 12pm midday.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.

properties.otherAdvice:
Mother's Day Classic fun run & walk is taking place at Parramatta Park from 7am.

Parramatta Park will be closed from 6am to 12pm. No parking or vehicle access will be available within the park during this time.

Traffic will be heavy on roads approaching and within Parramatta as attendees travel to and from the event. Allow extra travel time on Parramatta Rd, Church St, Victoria Rd, James Ruse Dr and Pennant Hills Rd.

Motorists should allow extra travel time and be aware of increased pedestrian activity on roads in the area

Major road closures will be in place on Sunday 4 May between 4am and 1pm in the Sydney CBD, The Rocks, Barangaroo and Pyrmont for the Runaway Sydney Half Marathon. The 10km course will start at 6.20am while Half Marathon runners will be released in waves from 6.40am. Both courses start on the Cahill Expressway at Macquarie St near Circular Quay and will end at The Domain Sydney by 12.30pm.   

Motorists are encouraged to avoid non-essential travel in the CBD and Pyrmont areas during the event as delays are expected. If you must drive, diversions will be in place so allow extra trave time and follow detour signs. 

Key closures: 

  • Sydney CBD – 4am to 12.30pm: Sections of Bridge St, Conservatorium Rd, Hunter St, Kent St and Macquarie St will be closed. The Cahill Expressway will be closed from The Domain Tunnel in both directions on the Circular Quay Overpass, and the Kent St on-ramp to the Sydney Harbour Bridge will also be closed. Motorists travelling towards the Eastern Distributor/Eastern Suburbs should use the Sydney Harbour Tunnel while the Cahill Expressway Overpass is closed. Traffic leaving the city can access the Sydney Harbour Bridge via Clarence St or Harbour St. Traffic can cross Macquarie St at Shakespeare Pl and Bent St before 5.30am and after 12pm. After 12pm, there is no access to or from Macquarie St; access to the Eastern Distributor will be available via William St. 
  • Pyrmont, Barangaroo & King St Wharf – 5am to 10.30am: the Western Distributor will be closed from Pyrmont to the CBD, including the Fig St and Pyrmont St on-ramps and the King St off-ramp. Sections of Sussex St, Erskine St, Hickson Rd, Kent St, King St and other local streets will be closed near King St Wharf and Barangaroo. Sections of Union St, Murray St, Pyrmont Bridge Rd, Pyrmont St, Darling Dr and surrounding local roads will be closed in Pyrmont. NOTE: there is no direct access from the Anzac Bridge to the Sydney Harbour Bridge. Citybound traffic on the Anzac Bridge will be detoured via the Bathurst St off-ramp. Citybound traffic from Pyrmont will be diverted via Harris St and local roads. 
  • Dawes Point, Millers Point, The Rocks & Barangaroo – 5am to 12pm: Sections of Hickson Rd, Towns Pl, Dalgety Rd, Pottinger St, Windmill St, Watson Rd and surrounding streets will be closed. Access to The Rocks is maintained via York St, Lang St and Harrington St. 
  • Pyrmont – 5am to 11am: Sections of Pirrama Rd, Bowman St, Darling Island Rd, Harris St, Bank St, Refinery Dr and surrounding local roads will be closed. 
  • Pyrmont – 5am to 11.30am: Pirrama Rd between Jones Bay Rd and Murray St; and Murray St between Union St and Pirrama Rd will be closed. 
  • Sydney CBD and The Domain Sydney – from 5am: Sections of College St, Prince Albert Rd, St Marys Rd, St James Rd, Hospital Rd, Bent St, Shakespeare Pl, Sir John Young Cres, Art Gallery Rd and Mrs Macquaries Rd will be closed. Some closures will lift from 9.30am, with all roads reopen by 1pm. 

Special event clearway parking restrictions will be in effect from 1am on various roads throughout the Sydney CBD, The Domain Sydney, Circular Quay, The Rocks, Millers Point, Barangaroo and Pyrmont. All clearways will be lifted by 12.30pm and all roads will be reopened by 1pm.   

Special event clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator. All clearways will be lifted by 12.30pm and all roads will be reopened by 1pm.

arrangementElements.title: Special Event Clearways

arrangementElements.html:
Motorists are advised to avoid King Street Wharf, Barangaroo, and Crown Sydney precincts between 5am and 12pm other than for residential or essential access. Police may restrict vehicle access along closed roads, including to residents and businesses.  

Circular Quay  

  • Access to Macquarie Street (North of Albert Street) will be via Albert Street while Macquarie Street is closed.  

Sydney Hospital & Hospital Road  

  • From 5am to 12.30pm, two-way access to Hospital Road via Prince Albert Road only, under traffic control. No access from Shakespeare Place.  

King Street Wharf and Barangaroo South  

  • From 6.30am to 10.30am, access to and from King Street Wharf, Cockle Bay Wharf and Barangaroo will be restricted to tenants/residents only. Access will be managed via Wheat Road from Harbour Street under traffic control; no access is available via Erskine Street or Sussex Street.  
  • Entry via Harbour Street, continue Western Distributor northbound, veer left into Wheat Road at the signposted exit for Erskine Street/CBD North.  
  • Light vehicles can exit the precinct via Wheat Road under contra-flow traffic control. Vehicles over 7 metres (including trucks, buses and coaches) will be unable to use the managed exit and will need to remain within the precinct until Erskine Street reopens.  
  • Before and after these times access is maintained via Erskine Street at Kent Street. We strongly advise motorists to avoid non-essential travel to or from these precincts between 6am and 10.30am as delays are expected.  

Millers Point & Barangaroo North  

  • Managed access to Kent Street properties as far north as Argyle Street, and High Street will be maintained by traffic control at Napoleon Street for the duration of the event. Kent Street southbound exit allowed for local traffic only.  
  • After 10am until roads reopen at 12pm, access to Barangaroo Reserve & car park, Dalgety Road and Bettington Street will be available via Kent Street, High Street, Argyle Place and Dalgety Road.  
  • Exiting Pottinger Street permitted via Windmill Street until 6am.  

The Rocks & Dawes Point   

  • Access maintained via Lang Street and Harrington Street throughout the event.  

Pyrmont  

  • Access to Murray Street properties/hotels and surrounding local roads will be permitted via Darling Drive under traffic control for light vehicles and coaches only (trucks not permitted). Note, coaches can only turn around via hotel driveways.  
  • No access available to Pyrmont Bridge Road or Star Casino from 5am to 10.30am. Access for taxis to Star Casino maintained via Jones Bay Road.   
  • Refinery Drive will be closed from 5am to 11am with exit permitted via Tambua Street before 6.45am and after 10.45am, only at Police discretion when there are safe gaps between runners. If you need access to your vehicle/property during these times, please plan ahead and relocate your vehicle prior.  
  • Access to and from The Star car park is via Pyrmont Street.  
  • No access from/to Pirrama Road from Wharf 7 and Wharf 10 access roads from 5am to 11.30am.  
  • No access to Murray Street from the Australian National Maritime Museum access road from 5am to 11.30am.  
  • Exit from driveways on Pyrmont Street properties between Bunn Lane and Murray Street permitted southbound under traffic control throughout the event.  
  • Resident access maintained to Bowman Street. Exit for local traffic via John Street only.

The Hawkesbury Cup Day will be held at Hawkesbury Racecourse in Clarendon on Saturday, gates open at 10:30am.

Heavy traffic is expected in Clarendon and surrounding suburbs approaching the racecourse.

Motorists should allow extra travel time on roads including Hawkesbury Valley Way, Blacktown Rd, The Northern Rd and Richmond Rd.

Attendees travelling to the show are encouraged to catch trains instead to avoid delays.

Caravan Camping Holiday Supershow at Rosehill Gardens. Start daily at 9:30m, finish Tuesday to Saturday at 5pm, and finish Sunday at 4pm.

Traffic may be heavier than usual on James Ruse Dr and Hassall St as attendees arrive and leave the event.

Motorists should allow extra travel time and be aware of increased pedestrian activity on local roads in the area.

A-League Men: Central Coast Mariners v Brisbane Roar at Central Coast Stadium. Kick off at 7:35pm and full time at around 9:35pm.

Traffic may be heavier than usual on roads approaching the stadium including on the Central Coast Hwy, Pacific Hwy, Brisbane Water Dr, Donnison St and Mann St as fans travel to and from the match.

Motorists should allow extra travel time and be aware of increased pedestrian activity on roads in the area.

Midnight Mafia at Sydney Showground, from 5pm until 11pm.

Traffic may be heavier than usual on roads approaching Sydney Olympic Park as attendees travel to and from the festival.

  • Motorists should allow extra travel time on roads including the M4 Mwy, Homebush Bay Dr, Concord Rd, Lane Cove Rd, Parramatta Rd, Centenary Dr and Silverwater Rd.
  • The precinct will be busier than usual with another concert being held at nearby Qudos Bank Arena at the same time.
  • If you have to drive, carpool with your group pre-book your parking online ahead of time to secure a space – available until 11:59pm the night before the event unless sold out prior. If you have pre-booked your parking, follow the directions of staff and have your parking ticket ready to show at the car park entry.

Sydney Olympic Park Authority may close local roads in the precinct to ensure pedestrian safety during events. View the interactive map for closure details.

On Sunday 4 May, multiple events are taking place in Moore Park including the AFL Sydney Derby at the SCG from 1.10pm. Attendees are urged to catch public transport and leave the car at home to avoid significant traffic delays and the high demand for parking.

  • Le Marché French Markets at the Entertainment Quarter from 9.30am until 2pm.
  • Major roads will also be closed in the Sydney CBD between 4am and 12.30pm for the annual Runaway Sydney Half Marathon. See details here.
  • Motorists are urged to avoid unnecessary travel in the area where possible.

Changed traffic conditions on Sunday 4 May:

  • Driver Avenue will be partially closed outside the SCG from 10.15am and will reopen once crowds have safely cleared the area.  
  • No through-traffic will be available on Driver Avenue.

Southbound motorists wanting to access Port Macquarie via Hastings River Drive will detour via the Port Macquarie Interchange and take the exit to Oxley Highway.

Northbound motorists wanting to access Telegraph Point will detour via:

  • Turn right to Taree using the underpass

  • Use the Telegraph Point exit Haydons Wharf Road.
